subject: Ontari Health — model evaluation & safety follow-up
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@ontarihealth.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@ontarihealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro / discovery — model fit & next steps

Hi Emily / Sanjay — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: automate patient messaging and clinical triage summaries for primary care clinics (short exchanges, many PHI touches).
- Throughput target: ~1k concurrent short messages (50–150 token responses) with 99th pct latency target under 200ms for text responses.
- Compliance: must run in customer VPC/private deployment due to PHI; KMS + audit logs required.
- Success criteria: match current human response accuracy on triage intent (>=92%) and zero high-severity hallucination incidents in evaluation suite.

Initial model recommendations (for evaluation)
- rw-llama-13b-q4f32 (Redwood-curated quantized variant) — strong balance of latency/cost for short-turn dialogs.
- rw-clinical-7b-ft (internal prototype) — fine-tuned on clinical SOAP notes; higher precision on clinical phrasing but needs safety vetting.
- Fallback: rw-7b-restrict (conservative response profile) for sensitive categories.

Planned evals / deliverables (we’ll provide)
- Prompt set: ontarihealth_prompt_set_v1.csv (attached) — 300 representative prompts split by sensitivity (PHI, triage, medication).
- Baseline benchmarks: latency/cost/quality (link below) for both recommended models.
- Safety/refusal checks: quick-run refusal bank and policy tests (Neha will share plan).
- Sandbox access: private tenant with sample dataset (scrubbed) for 2-week pilot.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll share the prompt set and a proposed mutual action plan (attached).
2) Emily/Sanjay — confirm a 60-min pilot kick-off on Wed or Thu this week.
3) Rohan (cc) will follow up with throughput/pricing scenarios once we confirm pilot timing.

Attachments: [Attachment: ontarihealth_prompt_set_v1.csv (text/csv)]
Links: https://redwood-eval.s3.amazonaws.com/ontarihealth/baseline-report.html

Happy to adjust — if you’d like the initial run to focus only on refusal behavior vs. the entire prompt set we can scope that down.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@ontarihealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@ontarihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Intro / discovery — model fit & next steps

Thanks Aisha — this is a helpful recap. A couple clarifying Qs before we lock in the pilot: 

1) PHI & auditability: can the sandbox we’ll be given run in our VPC with our KMS, and will you surface per-request audit logs (user id, timestamp, model version, response hash)? We need that for our privacy team.
2) Safety/guardrails: what does a "refusal" look like in practice? Can we see some example refusal templates or tone guides (e.g., explicit do-not-provide-differential-diagnosis vs. suggest-care pathways)?
3) Timeline: if we kick off Wed morning, can you deliver the baseline quality + safety report within 5 business days?

Also, I want to make sure we evaluate both the Llama-13b quantized candidate and the clinical-7b FT you mentioned. Cost vs. precision tradeoffs are key for us.

If Wed looks good, propose Wed 10:00am PT for the 60-min kick-off. Sanjay — does that work for you?

Best,
Emily
Product Owner, Conversational Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@ontarihealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: RE: Intro / discovery — model fit & next steps

Emily — quick note from the safety side on how we plan to approach the refusal/policy behavior evals and guardrails. High level: scope, tests, metrics, and deployment controls.

Scope & taxonomy
- Sensitive categories: PHI leakage, differential diagnosis requests, suicidal ideation/mental health, controlled substances, legal advice.
- Priority during pilot: PHI leakage and differential-diagnosis avoidance.

Test harness & artifacts
- refusal_prompt_bank.csv (attached) — ~250 prompts designed to trigger unsafe or disallowed outputs; includes expected refusal types (soft, redirect, explicit refusal).
- safety_test_plan.md (attached) — test cases, pass/fail criteria, and regression thresholds.
- automated golden-checks: reference responses + fuzzy match thresholds to detect hallucinations.

Metrics we’ll report
- refusal rate by category (per 1k prompts)
- unsafe output incidents (severity-graded) per 10k tokens
- false-positive refusals (legitimate requests incorrectly refused)
- latency impact when guardrails apply (ms overhead)

Guardrail options we can demo
1) Prompt-level filters + system instruction layer (high-precision refusals).
2) Post-generation classifiers (second-stage safety model) with probabilistic override.
3) Rule-based redaction for PHI-sensitive fields before generation.

Deployment & monitoring
- Canary: route 5–10% of traffic to the new model variant with safety logging enabled.
- Regression alerts: if unsafe incidents exceed 0.1% over baseline in any 24h window, automatic fallback to conservative model variant.

Compliance note: we can enable per-request audit logs (including model id, request hash, and KMS envelope id) inside the VPC deployment; that satisfies your privacy team’s ask.

Attachments: [Attachment: safety_test_plan.md (text/markdown)], [Attachment: refusal_prompt_bank.csv (text/csv)]
Links: https://app.redwood.ai/hubspot/ONT-2027-0042

If Wed 10am is confirmed we’ll start the initial run immediately after the call; estimated delivery for the baseline + safety report = 4 business days.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
